course_name_original: Desarrollo de un Sistema Mecatrónico Industrial – Proyecto de Semestre
course_name_en: Development of an Industrial Mechatronic System – Semester Project

learning_outcomes.text: Prepare technical specifications to formulate a problem in mechatronic engineering, maintaining a global and integrated vision and using prescriptive, procedural, or performance specifications as appropriate.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.

Evaluate the viability of new mechatronic products, based on their technological characteristics, manufacturing possibilities, and other socio-economic factors related to their possible implementation.

That students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving capacity in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

That students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments from incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
That students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
That students possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a way that must be largely self-directed or autonomous.

Know and use simulation software using finite elements to study the integral behavior (mechanical, static and dynamic, thermal, magnetic, electrical, etc.) of mechatronic elements and correctly interpret the results.
Discriminate the most critical components in a mechatronic system and justify their possible redesign from the control system's point of view.
Justify, with solid arguments, the different options for the automation of a mechatronic machine or technological process.
Know the regulations and apply quality management techniques and tools in the design of mechatronic equipment and systems.
Acquire knowledge, techniques, and skills that imply an increase in research and innovation potential and promote technology transfer to industry.
Select the material, dimension, and optimize the shape of mechatronic system elements, taking into account criteria of resistance, durability, and reliability.
Plan the manufacturing processes of mechatronic system components, considering the restrictions imposed by the manufacturing, assembly, and verification environment.
Plan the assembly, setup, and maintenance of mechatronic equipment or system.
Select the most appropriate programmable logic devices in each case for the design of mechatronic systems, manage their development systems, and design the interface stages that may be necessary.
Incorporate the necessary electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic sensors and actuators based on the characteristics of the mechatronic system, its specifications, and its integration.
Select electronic devices for instrumentation and control that allow conditioning and processing analog and digital signals from sensors and sent to typical actuators of a mechatronic system.
Identify the subcomponents of a technologically complex system, the interactions between them, and the effects and consequences of their possible redesign.
Design control systems of different complexity, from simple loops to distributed systems.
Apply the knowledge acquired in the first 3 semesters of the Master's to design, manufacture, and assemble an industrializable mechatronic system.
Be able to work in a group efficiently and coordinated, informing superiors appropriately and periodically.
Correctly document the technical-economic part of the project carried out.
Present and orally defend the project carried out.

syllabus_topics: Phases in prototype development: conceptual and detailed design
How to make the project presentation

assessment_methods.method: Project (group work, includes prototype, documentation: technical report, justifying calculations, wiring diagrams, plans, software documentation)
Oral tests (individual, assesses technical, theoretical, and practical knowledge, communication skills)
Skills scale (collaborative work aspects like integration, problem-solving, and formal aspects like punctuality)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, the project (70%), oral tests (20%), and skills scale (10%) are evaluated. The project is graded as a group, while oral tests and skills are individual. For extraordinary examinations, a mechatronic industrial project design is evaluated (75%), and an individual oral test (25%) is conducted where the developed project is presented and personal contribution is detailed. Differentiated evaluation follows the extraordinary examination criteria.
